### Emmy Income only user facing changes
- No changes, nothing to review!

### Emmy CE only user facing changes
- CE PDF Implementation [(#2035)](https://github.com/DSACMS/iv-cbv-payroll/pull/2035) - Daphne Gold [[FFS-4718]](https://jiraent.cms.gov/browse/FFS-4718)

- Hide language selector [(#2029)](https://github.com/DSACMS/iv-cbv-payroll/pull/2029) - Chris [[FFS-4642]](https://jiraent.cms.gov/browse/FFS-4642)

### Other/Maintenance (Not user facing)
- Bump rubocop, google.golang.org/grpc, vitest, sass, tornado, google.golang.org/grpc, postcss-selector-parser, postcss-cli, lookbook, webpack, rails_semantic_logger, bootsnap, mixpanel-ruby

- No consent pdf showing [(#2013)](https://github.com/DSACMS/iv-cbv-payroll/pull/2013) - Chris [[FFS-4596]](https://jiraent.cms.gov/browse/FFS-4596)

repos.name: super-changelog
repos.description: SuperChangelog is a tool for aggregating CHANGELOG.md files from individual repositories into one SUPERCHANGELOG

items: Initial release of super-changelog
Weekly pipeline (`run_weekly.py`) producing full and condensed summary PRs
Historical reporting with a custom date range
Org-agnostic design — works with any public GitHub organization
JSON data output for downstream dashboards and reporting
GitHub Ations workflow for automated weekly runs

commits.message:
chore(misc#351): frontend-env writes the auth token to public/config.js (#575)

## What

Updates `make frontend-env` for CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#722
(ztmf-misc#351): the local auth-bypass token now lands in
`ztmf-ui/public/config.js`, read by the app at runtime, instead of
`VITE_AUTH_TOKEN3` in `.env.development.local`, which nothing reads once
#722 is in. The env file keeps the vite proxy settings
(`VITE_CF_DOMAIN`, `VITE_IDP_ENABLED`); the retired `VITE_LOCAL_DEV`
flag is no longer written. Token generation is unchanged.

## Merge order

Landed after CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#722 (merged 2026-09-08). The order
mattered for safety, not convenience: #722 is what gitignores
`public/config.js`, and `public/` is tracked, so on the old ui main this
target would have left a live admin JWT untracked and unignored, one
`git add -A` from a public commit. It would also have broken local-dev
auth for anyone still on the env token.

## Verification

`make frontend-env` emits both files, and the generated token
authenticates against the local dev API (200 on `/api/v1/users/current`,
401 without it). No Go changes; the full local suite runs via the
pre-push hook.

commits.message:
fix(misc#297): add the READONLY_ADMIN mass-email group and widen massemails.group (#580)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#297. Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#653,
which reports the same 400 from the frontend side.

The EmailModal offers READONLY_ADMIN as a recipient group but
massEmailGroups had no such key, so the request failed validation.
Mack's call on the ticket was to add the backend group rather than drop
the option, since read-only admins are a small but distinct cohort at
CMS and likely at other OpDivs.

This adds a READONLY_ADMIN selector covering HHS_READONLY_ADMIN and
OPDIV_READONLY_ADMIN, mirroring how ADMIN covers the write tiers. ALL
still excludes every admin tier.

While wiring it up I found that massemails."group" was still the
VARCHAR(5) from migration 0011, so Save rejects any key longer than five
characters before recipients are resolved. SYSTEM_DELEGATE (15 chars)
hits this today and returns 500; I confirmed it against a clean dev
stack. Migration 0059 widens the column to VARCHAR(30), the same width
users.role got in 0035, so READONLY_ADMIN and SYSTEM_DELEGATE both save.
I also ran 0059 against a populated dev DB to check the upgrade path,
not just a fresh schema.

Behavior changes: POST /massemails with group READONLY_ADMIN goes from
400 to 201 and emails the read-only admin tiers. Group SYSTEM_DELEGATE
goes from 500 to 201. No API shape changes, openapi.yaml regenerates
with no drift.

Tests: unit tests pin that every group key fits the widened column and
that the READONLY_ADMIN query names exactly the two read-only roles.
Integration tests round-trip every key through Save (the check that
would have caught the width cap) and assert the READONLY_ADMIN audience
against the empire seed. Emberfall gains 201 cases for READONLY_ADMIN
and SYSTEM_DELEGATE; the test stack has no SMTP so the send goroutine
logs a dial error and nothing leaves.

Gate: make test-unit, make test-integration, and make test-e2e (221
passed, 0 failed) all green locally.

Not changed here: none of the role-based recipient queries filter
deleted users, so a deactivated admin or delegate still receives mail.
That predates this change and applies to every group, so I will file it
separately. Any service account carrying HHS_READONLY_ADMIN will be in
the READONLY_ADMIN audience.

commits.message:
Introduce tanstack query for datafetching (#727)

* feat(query): configure TanStack Query and application providers

Install TanStack Query and its development tools, then add a shared
QueryClient configured with a one-minute stale time, one retry, and no
window-focus refetching.

Wrap the application with QueryClientProvider and expose the closed-by-
default devtools only in development builds. Extend the shared test
renderer with a fresh no-retry client per render so cached server state
cannot leak between tests, and cover the application query defaults.

* refactor(api): centralize endpoint paths and query keys

Add canonical API path factories for every Axios endpoint so dynamic routes, query variants, and leading-slash conventions live in one place. Replace raw endpoint strings across views, utilities, auth flows, downloads, and mutations without altering their transport, cancellation, error handling, or `skipAuthHandling` behavior.

Add hierarchical TanStack Query keys that preserve response-shaping parameters and provide stable list and detail prefixes for cache invalidation. Centralize repeated score, export, and system-resource URL construction, and update affected tests to assert against the shared path factories.

* fix(query): retry only transient failures, never a 4xx

The blanket retry: 1 retried definitive server answers, and 401 was the
sharp case: the Axios interceptor reacts to it by navigating to the
login flow, so the retry fired a second doomed request into the
interceptor while that redirect was already underway. It also meant the
enrichment endpoint's expected 403/404 answers would each fire twice.

The default is now a function: one retry for network errors, non-Axios
errors and 5xx responses, where the next attempt can genuinely succeed;
no retries for any response below 500, which is the server saying
something rather than failing to answer.

* docs(api): record the URL-joining and encoding constraints in keys

Two facts a future reader needs before touching this module. The
leading-slash paths are safe only because Axios joins baseURL and path
by string concatenation; fetch or new URL semantics would resolve them
against the origin and silently drop /api/v1. And withQuery encodes
spaces as + where Axios params would write %20, which agrees today only
because no current parameter carries a space.

* build: fail production builds that bundle the query devtools

The devtools-absent-from-production contract cannot be a Jest test:
import.meta.env.DEV and NODE_ENV substitution happen at build time, so
a unit test only ever sees the development branch. This check runs
after vite build --mode production and greps the emitted bundles for
markers only the devtools carry.

Verified in both directions. The current build passes. Deleting the
main.tsx DEV gate alone does NOT trip it, because the package's main
entry already exports a no-op outside development; what does trip it,
exit 1, is importing the deliberate always-on
@tanstack/react-query-devtools/production entry, which is the realistic
way devtools would ever reach production.

* docs(keys): clarify URL encoding behavior in query parameters

* refactor(system-detail): fetch enrichment data with TanStack Query

Replace SystemEnrichmentCard's hand-written request effect and local loading, error, and response state with useQuery. Key enrichment reads by FISMA UID, forward Query's cancellation signal to Axios, and flatten the pipeline response envelope before exposing it to the existing card rendering.

Preserve the request-local auth bypass and existing UI behavior: 403 and 404 remain quiet empty states, unexpected failures retain the failed-load message, and the ISSO update PUT remains imperative. Extend the component tests to verify skipAuthHandling and cancellation when the query unmounts.

* feat(query): standardize error handling and document data fetching

Add a shared QueryCache error callback that suppresses interceptor-handled auth errors, cancellations, unobserved requests, and queries with inline error states. Normalize other query failures through `parseApiError` and `notify` once, with duplicate prevention keyed by the query hash.

Expose a `QueryClient` factory so production and component tests share the same cache behavior while tests can disable retries. Add integration coverage for a 401 raised inside a query function, including redirect behavior, retry suppression, and protection against duplicate toasts. Pin `skipAuthHandling` at all five sanctioned call sites.

Document query-key conventions, cancellation, invalidation, query and mutation usage, Axios interoperability, and session-bootstrap exceptions. Fix formatting in the production devtools assertion script.

* fix(query): address review findings on data-fetching migration

TanStack Query retains the last successful `data` payload when a background refetch fails, populating `error` at the same time. `SystemEnrichmentCard` evaluated `error` in isolation, replacing populated Insights panels with red error text during failed refreshes. While `refetchOnWindowFocus` is disabled, `refetchOnReconnect` remains active, making network interruptions reaching two 5xx responses sufficient to trigger this state. Main avoided this behavior by omitting background refetches entirely and relying on an effect keyed on `fismaUid`. The guard now checks `error && !notFound && !enrichment`, and `docs/data-fetching.md` documents this retained-data behavior to ensure consistent implementation across remaining views.

This commit addresses additional items identified during review:

* **`apiPaths.scores.list` path enforcement:** Restores rejection on missing identifiers. Because `withQuery` drops `undefined` values, omitting a system ID stripped the filter parameter and returned scores for all systems in the data call. Callers folded these results into a function/option ID-keyed map, yielding invalid data instead of throwing a explicit error. `export` and `questions` narrow parameter types to prevent `undefined` values from reaching URL builders.
* **`FismaTable` export URL parameter handling:** Prevents `FismaTable` from substituting active data call IDs into export URLs. `exportCallId` evaluates to `null` when selections span multiple data calls; substituting values via `??` generated downloads containing mismatched data call responses. While disabled button states cover primary interaction paths, the click handler now exits early on `null` values.
* **`keys.ts` docblock correction:** Corrects `keys.ts` documentation stating `baseURL` is `/api/v1/`. The relative value `api/v1/` allows single build artifacts to serve behind PR environment prefixes. Integration test mock configurations are updated to match.
* **Cache key identifier normalization:** Normalizes identifiers in cache keys using `keyId` string conversion so `detail(42)` and `detail('42')` resolve to identical cache entries. This prevents invalidation mismatches caused by mixed string route parameters and numeric call sites.
* **Devtools dependency isolation:** Moves devtools to `devDependencies` and transitions loading to dynamic imports. Static imports added devtools to runtime dependency graphs evaluated by Snyk and SBOM scanners. Vite converts the `import.meta.env.DEV` ternary to `null` during production builds, omitting devtools chunks from output.
* **Devtools build assertion coverage:** Adds devtools build assertions to `build:dev`. Previous execution was restricted to `build:prod` within production orchestration pipelines, allowing regressions to pass merge validation. Assertion failure messaging now specifies the always-on `/production` entry point and packaging requirements.
* **Test suite corrections:** Fixes two questionnaire test suites matching `url.startsWith('scores')` against leading-slash paths, which previously passed by returning empty default payloads. Corrects `delegates.test.ts` mock parameters where test descriptions asserted capability-off rejections while mock setup returned 201 responses.

Refs #619

commits.message:
feat(misc#340): serialize deploy workflows with concurrency groups (#729)

* feat(misc#340): serialize deploy workflows with concurrency groups

Every deploying workflow declares a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress
false: ref-keyed for dev, impl, and the manual deploys, environment-keyed for
prod, plus a deploy-<env> job group on the ui job so bucket syncs queue
instead of racing.

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#321.

* feat(misc#340): deep queue on the deploy groups, merged-keyed prod group

queue: max on deploy-dev and deploy-impl so a third PR queues behind the
second instead of evicting its pending deploy (which left that PR with no dev
deployment and unmergeable). The prod group is keyed on
github.event.pull_request.merged so unmerged closes cannot evict a pending
prod deploy.
commits.author: cameron testerman

commits.message:
hotfix(misc#386): carry the system id from System Info to the questionnaire and refuse ambiguous acronyms (#734)

The questionnaire route is keyed on the acronym, which is not unique. The
System Info Questionnaire button linked by acronym alone, so for systems
sharing one it opened the lowest-id match and answers were saved against
that system. The button now navigates with the fismasystemid in route state
on a plain click, leaving modified clicks to the anchor, and acronym
resolution returns nothing when more than one system matches, with a
warning in place of a silent guess.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#386
